rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.desc: Students must fulfill the WIM requirement that aligns with their subplan.

children.name: WIM for Students in Social Systems Subplan
children.desc:
Most students pursuing the Data Science B.A. with the social systems subplan will complete the Data Science Practicum (DATASCI 192A/B), which double-counts to satisfy both the capstone and WIM requirements.
In special instances, students can apply to fulfill the capstone requirement through conducting an independent data science research project under the supervision of a professor (see capstone requirement for more details), in which case they must take DATASCI 120 to satisfy the WIM requirement.

children.name: WIM for Students in Artistic and Cultural Analysis Subplan
children.desc: All students pursuing the Artistic and Cultural Analysis subplan must complete the following as their WIM.

rules.name: Capstone
rules.desc: The capstone is a culminating experience completed during senior year. Students must fulfill the capstone requirement that aligns with their subplan. In addition, each student must participate in the final Capstone Showcase in spring of their senior year.

children.name: Capstone for Students in Social Systems Subplan
Data Science Practicum
children.desc: Most students pursuing the Data Science & Social Systems B.A. will complete the Data Science Practicum (DATASCI 192A/B) for their capstone, which double-counts to satisfy both the capstone and WIM requirements.

children.name: Independent Research Project
children.desc:
In special instances, completing DATASCI 120 and an independent research project in data science could also be considered for the capstone requirement; the project must be pre-approved by the program directors, substantially use techniques from upper-division Data Science coursework, connect to a social issue (typically related to the student’s pathway), and be completed during senior year.

• By the final study list deadline of autumn quarter during senior year, students should join the Canvas page for Independent Research Projects.

• During autumn quarter of senior year, students should find a professor who agrees to supervise the research project.

• By the last day of classes of autumn quarter, students must complete the Proposal to Use Independent Research for Data Science & Social Systems B.A. Capstone form, have it approved by the research advisor, and submit it to the Canvas page for Independent Research Projects. Approval must be obtained from the program directors through this process.

• Students should enroll in course (independent study) for a letter grade with the supervising professor in every quarter until they finish conducting the research and creating the report/poster.

• To complete the capstone, the student must submit a final report and approval form signed by their research advisor.
Students who use an independent research project to fulfill the capstone requirement will need to take DATASCI 120 (Data Narratives) to fulfill the WIM requirement. DATASCI 120 complements independent research, and it can be taken before or concurrently with working on the project.

children.desc: All students pursuing the Artistic and Cultural Analysis subplan must complete the following as their capstone.

rules.name: Pathway
rules.desc: The pathway is an opportunity for students to develop specific expertise on a topic they are passionate about and where data science methods and approaches have something compelling to offer. Students must choose one of the following pathways or develop their own, with guidance and approval from the program.

children.name: Brains & Behavior
children.desc:
Complete seven total courses, at least two from each category (Foundation, Intersection, Context).
Courses must span at least two social science disciplines (communication, economics, political science, psychology, and sociology).
To support students in selecting balanced pathway coursework, students will be required to meet with the data science team to discuss their planned pathway courses and receive final program approval.

children.name: Foundation Courses
children.desc: Foundation Courses introduce students to the social sciences through survey or introductory courses relevant to the pathway.

children.name: Intersection Courses
children.desc: Intersection Courses give students the opportunity to work with data or apply computational methods within their pathway topic.
children.notes:
To use DATASCI 120 toward the pathway, students must submit the Request to use DATASCI 120 for Pathway form and receive program approval.
To use DATASCI 192D toward the pathway, students must complete their capstone project with an organization that aligns with their pathway and receive program approval.
To use DATASCI 199 toward the pathway, students must enroll for at least 2 units and conduct research relevant to the pathway under supervision of a faculty advisor.

children.name: Context Courses
children.desc: Context Courses provide additional knowledge on topics or methods used in this area of study. This pathway covers courses from Neuroscience and Cognitive Science.
